pathway.title: Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The credit is strong today but weakening in direction, and the cause is financial policy more than trading. Total debt rose from 1.45x reported EBITDA at FY2025 to 1.77x over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 while earnings still covered cash interest 9.46x, and the StormTrap purchase and the repurchase after quarter end would lift net leverage from 1.60x to 2.30x pro forma. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

Business quality is strong but not defensive. The Adjusted EBITDA margin was 31.97% over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and the Wastewater segment earned 43.59% against 28.89% in Stormwater in FY2026, yet sales follow construction and housing activity, and the ten largest customers took about 50% of FY2026 net sales, with many on no long-term arrangement. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 48; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Cash generation is a strength with room to flex. Free cash flow was 59.12% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2026 against 41.45% in FY2025, it covered trailing cash interest 5.49 times, and capital expenditures of USD 249,766 thousand in FY2026 are guided to about USD 200 million in FY2027, 19.93% lower; cash taxes also fell 20.26% in FY2026. Basis: calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F05; calculation F20; calculation F09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 134

Liquidity and maturities leave no near-term funding pressure. Liquidity was USD 891.88 million at 2026-09-30, only 2.87% of principal falls due before fiscal 2030, the first bond matures on 2030-07-15, and the USD 750 million revolver and the term loan run to 2031-02-27 and 2033-02-28; the February 2026 refinancing shows access to both the loan and the bond markets. Basis: calculation F10; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 119–122; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The primary downside path is volume, and its first signs are already visible. Net sales excluding NDS fell 4.50% in the September 2026 quarter after rising 9.22% in the June quarter, domestic pipe sales fell 7.59% in the September quarter, and the Stormwater segment margin fell 1.48 percentage points to 29.49%, with higher material and transportation costs cited for Stormwater, so operating leverage and cost pass-through are already under test. Basis: calculation F13; calculation F15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Financial policy is the swing factor. Cash returned to shareholders was 112.22% of free cash flow in the first half of FY2027 and acquisitions plus shareholder returns were 159.53% of free cash flow over FY2025 and FY2026, no leverage target is stated, and governance risk is medium because no named sponsor and a dispersed holder base remove extraction risk but not the board's own discretion. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

The one maintenance covenant is a springing test that may become live. The 4.25x senior secured net leverage test applies only when revolver exposure exceeds USD 262,500 thousand, 35% of commitments, so a StormTrap purchase funded mainly from the revolver could switch it on; its definition and the issuer's ratio are not supplied, so headroom is not established. Basis: calculation F12; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Integration is a second downside path. Goodwill and identified intangibles are 78.51% of the NDS price, NDS was left out of the internal control assessment, five of its entities were held for sale on acquisition, and a fourth acquisition in two years, StormTrap, is pending, so earnings from the purchases are not yet visible. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: A first strength is cash generation with flexibility. Free cash flow was 59.12% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2026, 50.69% before working-capital movements, it covered trailing cash interest 5.49 times, and capital expenditure is guided down from USD 249,766 thousand to about USD 200 million, so debt service has a wide cushion and a lever in a downturn. Basis: calculation F01; calculation F23; calculation F05; calculation F20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1)

A second strength is margin level and mix: the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 31.97% over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and Wastewater earned 43.59% against 28.89% in Stormwater, which gives earnings room to absorb a volume or price shock before interest cover is threatened. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

A third strength is liquidity with back-ended maturities: USD 891.88 million of liquidity at 2026-09-30, only 2.87% of principal due before fiscal 2030 and no bond until 2030-07-15, so refinancing risk is remote for at least two years. Basis: calculation F10; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 121; Financial foundation (CP-1)

A fourth strength is market position and conversion: management describes a national footprint in a fragmented industry and a continuing shift from concrete, steel and PVC to thermoplastic pipe; this is management language, but the 64 plants, regulatory approvals and 41 distribution centers are documented and support share retention. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49

A fifth strength is moderate leverage today: net debt was 1.60x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, which is 2.30x pro forma for the StormTrap purchase (agreement dated 2026-10-01) and the repurchase after quarter end, still far below the 4.25x springing covenant level on a different definition. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; Financial foundation (CP-1)

A first weakness is volume sensitivity with operating leverage: net sales excluding NDS fell 4.50% in the September 2026 quarter, domestic pipe sales fell 7.59%, and the Stormwater segment margin fell 1.48 percentage points, which shows fixed plant cost and a lagged resin pass-through turning a modest volume fall into margin loss. Basis: calculation F15; Business & governance (CP-1A)

A second weakness is financial policy: cash returned to shareholders was 112.22% of free cash flow in the first half of FY2027 and acquisitions plus shareholder returns were 159.53% of free cash flow over FY2025 and FY2026, with no leverage target stated, so the next move can add debt without any limit creditors can see. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

A third weakness is customer concentration: the two largest distributors took 25.8% of FY2026 net sales and the ten largest customers about 50%, many without long-term arrangements, so one customer decision can move volume and price within a quarter. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A)

A fourth weakness is acquisition integration and asset quality: goodwill and identified intangibles are 78.51% of the NDS price, NDS was left out of the internal control assessment, five NDS entities were held for sale on acquisition and StormTrap is the fourth purchase in two years, so recovery of value from deals is not yet visible in earnings. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; Business & governance (CP-1A)

A fifth weakness is resin exposure with a pass-through lag: resin is the main variable input, the filing says increases may lag costs and may not be passed on where competing materials cap prices, and the September 2026 gross margin was 1.11 percentage points lower than a year earlier. Basis: calculation F18; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 50

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The pending transaction is the purchase of StormTrap Investments LLC under a definitive agreement entered on 2026-10-01 for approximately USD 530 million, funded by cash on hand and existing credit line capacity, with closing expected in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. The supplied filings do not show the agreement terms, StormTrap's earnings or any closing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43

The completed transaction that reshaped the company is NDS, bought on 2026-02-02 for USD 984.9 million, or USD 972.5 million net of cash, primarily from cash on hand. 78.51% of the price is goodwill and identified intangibles, NDS added USD 48.8 million of net sales in its first two months, and five of its entities were held for sale on acquisition. Basis: calculation A62; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 105–106; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

New debt was raised on 2026-02-27, 25 days after NDS closed: a USD 600 million term loan due 2033 and USD 500 million of senior notes due 2034, alongside a revolver raised from USD 600 million to USD 750 million and extended to 2031. The new debt refinanced the earlier term loan of USD 413.25 million and redeemed the USD 350 million of senior notes due 2027 at par. The supplied pages call the new notes senior but do not say whether they are secured or how they rank against the secured bank debt, and the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30. Basis: calculation A77; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 119–120; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

Shareholder transactions run alongside: a USD 1.0 billion repurchase authorization of February 2026 with USD 563.2 million left after the shares bought since 2026-09-30, and a quarterly dividend raised to USD 0.20 per share. Basis: calculation A58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Advanced Drainage Systems is releveraging: net debt reached 1.60x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 from 0.92x at FY2025, and the pending StormTrap purchase and continuing buybacks would lift it further, so creditors face rising leverage on a business that covers cash interest 9.46x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage rose because the NDS acquisition was funded from cash on hand and new borrowing while reported earnings barely moved. Between FY2025 and FY2026 gross debt at balance-sheet value rose USD 350,300 thousand and cash fell USD 240,307 thousand, which lifted net debt from 0.92x to 1.59x of reported EBITDA, while EBITDA itself grew only 0.72%. At 2026-09-30 the multiple was 1.60x on trailing EBITDA of USD 912,734 thousand: gross debt was little changed at USD 1,611,197 thousand against USD 1,611,823 thousand in March, but cash was USD 69,767 thousand lower.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trailing EBITDA both flatters and understates the leverage picture. It holds NDS for only 240 days of the 365 days in the window, and the annual report's pro forma net sales for FY2026 with NDS owned all year were USD 239,316 thousand above reported net sales; the filings give no pro forma EBITDA, so run-rate EBITDA is probably higher than the trailing figure. The issuer's EBITDA also counts USD 35,968 thousand of interest income, other income and equity income, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortisation alone net debt is 1.66x rather than 1.60x.

fields.value: Interest cover is ample but easing. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 9.46x on a trailing basis against 10.05x in FY2026 and 9.71x in FY2025, because interest expense grew 18.23% and cash interest paid 22.16% in the first half of fiscal 2027 on the larger debt stack, while trailing EBITDA grew only 4.31% over FY2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is strong, but shareholder distributions now absorb all of it. Free cash flow was USD 359,489 thousand in the six months to 2026-09-30, down 9.86% as operating cash flow fell USD 51,596 thousand on working capital; buybacks and dividends took USD 403,428 thousand, USD 43,939 thousand more than free cash flow. A further USD 114.1 million was spent on repurchases after the quarter end, leaving about USD 563,195 thousand of the authorisation unused.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and maturities are back-ended. At 2026-09-30 liquidity was USD 891.88 million: cash of USD 153,245 thousand plus USD 738,635 thousand of undrawn revolver after USD 11,365 thousand of letters of credit, with the revolver maturing 2031-02-27. Only USD 7,955 thousand of debt is current. Scheduled principal at 2026-03-31 is no more than USD 32,675 thousand a year until fiscal 2031, when USD 506 million falls due, including the USD 500 million 2030 senior notes, followed by USD 1,071.5 million after that, which includes the 2034 senior notes and the balance of the term loan due 2033-02-28.

fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are modest against earnings but real. Finance leases of USD 161,909 thousand sit on their own balance-sheet lines, inside the issuer's own 1.6x measure but outside ours; operating lease liabilities were USD 74,199 thousand at 2026-03-31; redeemable KSOP shares of USD 69,045 thousand are mezzanine equity with a put right only if the stock stops being listed; and open equipment orders were about USD 80 million. The filings describe no defined-benefit pension, factoring or supplier finance programme and no fixed-price purchase commitment, and the guarantee of the South American joint venture's debt, capped at USD 5.5 million with nothing outstanding, expires 2026-12-31.

fields.value: Underlying trading softened in the latest quarter. Excluding NDS, net sales in the quarter to 2026-09-30 fell 4.50% and Adjusted EBITDA slipped 0.25% even though NDS added USD 77.3 million of sales, with the Adjusted EBITDA margin at 32.25% against 33.81% a year earlier; over the six months, excluding NDS, net sales still rose 2.28%. The issuer attributes the quarter to lower volumes in pipe, allied products and wastewater, partly offset by price and mix, so NDS is masking a weaker organic quarter, though the six-month base is still up.

fields.value: Two reported items conflict between filings and are logged rather than reconciled. The June quarterly report put the loss on the Teco sale at USD 4.0 million for the quarter while the September report gives USD 3.0 million for the six months, and the term loan's administrative agent is named differently in the September quarterly report and the annual report; neither changes any debt, cash or EBITDA figure used here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is cash generation and the unused revolver. Trailing free cash flow of USD 529,952 thousand is 5.49 times trailing cash interest paid, the USD 750 million revolver is undrawn, and the issuer states that it complied with its covenants at 2026-09-30. The one maintenance test, a 4.25x senior secured net leverage ratio, applies only when revolver exposure exceeds 35% of commitments, so it does not apply while exposure sits far below that level. Reported EBITDA was also held back by restructuring and transaction costs of USD 48,299 thousand and USD 40,805 thousand in FY2026; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA net debt is 1.40x and Adjusted EBITDA grew 8.29% in FY2026.

A weaker view would follow if StormTrap were funded mainly from the revolver: cash of USD 153,245 thousand at 2026-09-30 would, if no further cash were generated, leave USD 376,755 thousand to borrow, above the USD 262.5 million of revolver exposure at which the 4.25x test starts to apply, and the filings give neither the covenant definition nor the issuer's ratio, so headroom could not be confirmed.

fields.value: Business & governance for Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc. (issuer wms-1604028), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: business model and revenue mix, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation, issuer history and the pending StormTrap acquisition, from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness analysis. Sponsor behaviour is assessed only where the filings document it, and no sponsor is named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The document dates are the signature dates the documents print. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Advanced Drainage Systems has no named sponsor, so creditors depend on management's own financial policy, and that policy now spends more than the business generates, on acquisitions and shareholder returns, which makes covenant terms the filings do not show the real protection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating base is strong, with segment margins of 28.89% in Stormwater and 43.59% in Wastewater, but growth is bought: net sales rose 5.03% in fiscal 2026 and 1.54% without the two acquisitions, and fell 4.50% in the September 2026 quarter without NDS. Two distributors take 25.8% of sales, and the pending USD 530 million StormTrap purchase and the USD 114.1 million of shares bought back since quarter end together equal 72.22% of the cash and revolver availability at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is medium, and it comes from financial policy rather than control. No named sponsor and a dispersed holder base remove the usual extraction risk, but a policy that spends more than free cash flow, a repeating acquisition pace and missing board and credit documents keep it from low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No investor controls the company and no sponsor is named, so sponsor extraction and sponsor support are not in play and the discipline that matters is the board's own. Directors, officers and principal stockholders together hold about 16% of the shares and about 22% of the votes counting the employee retirement plan, and the filings name Canada Pension Plan Investment Board as party to 2021 shareholder and registration rights agreements without stating its holding or rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is elastic rather than conservative, and no stated leverage target bounds it. Over fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026 acquisitions and shareholder returns together took 159.53% of free cash flow while the cash balance fell, and in the first half of fiscal 2027 buybacks and dividends alone took 112.22%, against 26.01% in fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A55; calculation A51; calculation A48; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported growth overstates demand: fiscal 2026 net sales rose 5.03% but 1.54% once NDS and the full-year effect of Orenco are removed, and the first half of fiscal 2027 rose 2.28% without NDS, made up of a rise of 9.22% in the June quarter and a fall of 4.50% in the September quarter, when volume in pipe and allied products fell while price and mix improved. The filings do not explain the swing, so the September decline cannot yet be called a trend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is moving from resin-linked pipe toward allied products and wastewater, which should dampen resin exposure if acquired margins hold. Domestic pipe fell from 50.87% of segment sales in fiscal 2025 to 43.50% in the first half of fiscal 2027, while allied products, which now include NDS, rose to 29.73%; Wastewater earned a segment margin of 43.59% against 28.89% in Stormwater in fiscal 2026 and supplied 30.70% of segment profit on 22.70% of segment sales, so a weak housing market would cut earnings by more than its sales share suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is the structural business risk: two distributors took 25.8% of fiscal 2026 net sales and 27.0% in fiscal 2025, most sales run through distributors, and demand is seasonal, higher between April and September. A change in volumes or terms at one of them would reach earnings before any offset, and the filings give no contract terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquired assets are intangible-heavy and partly for resale, so little of the price is backed by physical assets. Goodwill and identified intangibles are 78.51% of the USD 984.9 million paid for NDS, five NDS entities were held for sale on acquisition, two were sold in July 2026, and the first half carried a USD 29,818 thousand loss from classifying the rest as held for sale.

fields.value: Reporting quality supports monitoring, with one open point: the annual report was signed 51 days after year end, the audit opinions were unqualified and internal control was effective, yet NDS, which carried 23% of total assets, was left out of the control assessment, so the largest recent addition has not been through a full control cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capacity to add debt grew in February 2026 and willingness to spend cash is shown by action, but the size of the capacity is not supplied. The amendment allows incremental facilities of up to the greater of USD 350 million or 100% of consolidated EBITDA and amended certain baskets, while the definitions that size them are missing, so capacity is described and not calculated; no priming, exchange or other creditor-adverse transaction is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is cash generation and balance-sheet room. Free cash flow was USD 569,288 thousand in fiscal 2026, liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 891,880 thousand with the revolver undrawn, no bond matures before 2030, and shareholder payouts in the first half of fiscal 2027 were met from cash and operating cash flow with no revolver borrowings. A cut in buybacks, or a StormTrap closing funded mainly from cash flow with the revolver largely undrawn, would move the view toward low governance risk.

fields.value: What would worsen the view is a debt-funded buyback or a revolver draw large enough to take exposure above 35% of commitments, which switches on the springing covenant; a further large acquisition before StormTrap is integrated; another quarter of falling volume excluding NDS; or credit documents showing wide payout and debt baskets. What would improve it is a stated leverage target, a proxy statement showing an independent board with credit-relevant oversight, and credit documents that cap payouts and additional debt.

fields.value: | 1 | Releveraging through acquisitions and buybacks | Net debt over reported EBITDA of 1.60x at 2026-09-30 and 2.30x pro forma for the StormTrap purchase and the repurchase after quarter end; cash returned to shareholders was 112.22% of free cash flow in the first half of FY2027; no leverage target is stated | Discretionary uses of cash and revolver capacity rise with each deal and buyback, and the board can scale either up | Higher leverage and a smaller cash cushion into a softer volume cycle; covenant test may become live | Negative | High |

fields.value: | 2 | Cash generation and interest cover | Free cash flow was 59.12% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2026 (50.69% before working capital) and covered trailing cash interest 5.49 times; reported EBITDA covered cash interest 9.46x | Strong conversion with low interest burden and flexible capital expenditure | Wide cushion for debt service; supports deleveraging if payouts slow | Positive | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc. (issuer wms-1604028), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: an integrated view of business quality, cash generation, leverage, liquidity, refinancing and financial policy, built from the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses and the supplied filings. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The document dates are the signature dates the documents print. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Advanced Drainage Systems has a strong credit profile, with high margins, strong free cash flow and no bond maturity before 2030, but management is spending that strength on acquisitions and buybacks, so rising leverage, not liquidity, is the risk for creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F01; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 121; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was 1.60x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, and 2.30x pro forma for the StormTrap purchase (agreement dated 2026-10-01) and the share repurchase after the quarter end (no day stated), which are 2.18x and 1.72x taken alone. Net sales excluding NDS fell 4.50% in the September 2026 quarter, so the main downside path is weaker volume meeting higher leverage while covenant terms are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit is strong today but weakening in direction, and the cause is financial policy more than trading. Total debt rose from 1.45x reported EBITDA at FY2025 to 1.77x over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 while earnings still covered cash interest 9.46x, and the StormTrap purchase and the repurchase after quarter end would lift net leverage from 1.60x to 2.30x pro forma.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business quality is strong but not defensive. The Adjusted EBITDA margin was 31.97% over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and the Wastewater segment earned 43.59% against 28.89% in Stormwater in FY2026, yet sales follow construction and housing activity, and the ten largest customers took about 50% of FY2026 net sales, with many on no long-term arrangement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 48; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is a strength with room to flex. Free cash flow was 59.12% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2026 against 41.45% in FY2025, it covered trailing cash interest 5.49 times, and capital expenditures of USD 249,766 thousand in FY2026 are guided to about USD 200 million in FY2027, 19.93% lower; cash taxes also fell 20.26% in FY2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F05; calculation F20; calculation F09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 134

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities leave no near-term funding pressure. Liquidity was USD 891.88 million at 2026-09-30, only 2.87% of principal falls due before fiscal 2030, the first bond matures on 2030-07-15, and the USD 750 million revolver and the term loan run to 2031-02-27 and 2033-02-28; the February 2026 refinancing shows access to both the loan and the bond markets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F10; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 119–122; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is volume, and its first signs are already visible. Net sales excluding NDS fell 4.50% in the September 2026 quarter after rising 9.22% in the June quarter, domestic pipe sales fell 7.59% in the September quarter, and the Stormwater segment margin fell 1.48 percentage points to 29.49%, with higher material and transportation costs cited for Stormwater, so operating leverage and cost pass-through are already under test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F13; calculation F15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor. Cash returned to shareholders was 112.22% of free cash flow in the first half of FY2027 and acquisitions plus shareholder returns were 159.53% of free cash flow over FY2025 and FY2026, no leverage target is stated, and governance risk is medium because no named sponsor and a dispersed holder base remove extraction risk but not the board's own discretion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one maintenance covenant is a springing test that may become live. The 4.25x senior secured net leverage test applies only when revolver exposure exceeds USD 262,500 thousand, 35% of commitments, so a StormTrap purchase funded mainly from the revolver could switch it on; its definition and the issuer's ratio are not supplied, so headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F12; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Integration is a second downside path. Goodwill and identified intangibles are 78.51% of the NDS price, NDS was left out of the internal control assessment, five of its entities were held for sale on acquisition, and a fourth acquisition in two years, StormTrap, is pending, so earnings from the purchases are not yet visible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern about policy is the size of the cushion it has not yet used. Free cash flow of USD 569,288 thousand in FY2026 covers cash interest comfortably, liquidity is USD 891.88 million with the revolver undrawn, buybacks in the first half of FY2027 were met from cash and operating cash flow, and the pro forma 2.30x counts no StormTrap earnings and only part-year NDS earnings, so run-rate leverage is probably lower than shown. A smaller buyback, or StormTrap earnings that prove large against its price of about USD 530 million, would move the view toward stable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: What would worsen the view is a debt-funded buyback or a revolver draw above USD 262,500 thousand, a second quarter of falling sales excluding NDS, a further resin spike that the company cannot pass on, or credit documents with wide payout and debt baskets. What would improve it is a stated leverage target, StormTrap earnings and a closing funded largely from cash flow, a recovery of volume in the December 2026 quarter, and covenant definitions showing wide headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, market price or peer data is supplied, so strength is judged against the issuer's own history and stated facts and not against rated peers or trading levels; a peer comparison could move the business quality judgement either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - StormTrap and NDS earnings are not disclosed, so the leverage path is bounded by the stated pro forma figures and not by run-rate EBITDA; the sign of the error is probably favourable, but it cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside path is built from observed quarterly changes and the issuer's stated levers, not from a forecast, because no management outlook beyond capital expenditure is published; it shows sequence and direction, not a calibrated loss of earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Sector datapoints such as housing starts, non-residential construction spending and resin spreads are not in the supplied documents, so the cycle position is inferred from the issuer's own volume and price disclosures; a different sector reading could change the revenue durability judgement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Advanced Drainage Systems makes thermoplastic corrugated pipe and related water management products for stormwater and onsite wastewater, sold mainly through distributors into non-residential, residential, infrastructure and agriculture construction. It reports two segments, Stormwater at 78.59% and Wastewater at 21.41% of FY2026 external net sales, and runs 64 manufacturing plants and 41 distribution centers that give it a national delivery footprint, which supports cost and service against regional competitors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-flow visibility is moderate rather than high. Orders are short-cycle with many customers on no long-term arrangement, sales are higher in the April to September half (55.08% of FY2026 net sales fell in the first half), and no backlog is published; against that, the customer base is large and the products are specified into long-lived drainage and septic installations, so debt service rests on strong margins and cash conversion rather than on contracted revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is publicly held and no sponsor or parent is named: directors, officers and principal stockholders hold about 16% of the shares and about 22% of the votes counting the employee retirement plan, and charter provisions make a takeover harder. Creditors therefore face no sponsor-style recapitalisation risk and have no sponsor to turn to for support, and policy is set by a board whose independence and credit orientation are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The borrower is the parent, and StormTech, Infiltrator Water Technologies and Orenco Systems guarantee the credit agreement; the joint ventures are small, with the issuer owning 51% of ADS Mexicana and 63% of EQ TruePointe One and guaranteeing at most USD 5.5 million of the South American joint venture's debt, which expires on 2026-12-31. The supplied pages disclose no holding company layer or unrestricted subsidiary designation, but the credit documents that would define them are not supplied and the ranking and security of the senior notes are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical, short-cycle and concentrated, with partly lagged pass-through pricing. Demand follows non-residential and residential construction, infrastructure funding and farm income, which the issuer links to credit availability and interest rates; the ten largest customers took about 50% of FY2026 net sales and the two largest distributors 25.8%, so volume risk sits with a few buyers who can switch suppliers on short notice. The annual report states directly what the Business & governance analysis recorded as not described, that many customers have no long-term arrangement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is real but lagged. In the September 2026 quarter price and mix improved while volume fell in both pipe and allied products, the issuer says allied products are less sensitive to resin prices, and it argues that conversion from concrete, steel and PVC to thermoplastic pipe continues as regulatory approvals widen; that conversion is management's view, and it protects volume only while thermoplastic stays price-competitive with the alternatives.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Resin is the main variable input: the company buys more than 1.0 billion pounds a year from about 450 suppliers, had no fixed-price purchase commitments outstanding at 2026-09-30 and relies on selling-price increases to recover cost, which the filing says can lag. Plants carry substantial fixed costs, so margin falls faster than sales when volume drops: against the prior-year quarter the September 2026 gross margin was 1.11 percentage points lower and the Stormwater segment margin 1.48 percentage points lower, even with NDS added.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F18; calculation F15; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wastewater held its margin at 44.89% against 44.91% a year earlier, which locates the pressure in Stormwater, where the NDS mix and the resin-linked pipe and allied business both sit. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through recycled resin, diesel hedging and price increases, but a combined volume decline and resin spike would outrun those defences, since the filing warns that sharp resin rises can reach levels that cannot be fully passed through because of competing-product pricing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F16; calculation F17; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA converts to free cash flow well, but the year-to-year improvement is mostly working capital. Free cash flow was 59.12% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2026 against 41.45% in FY2025, yet working capital added USD 81,171 thousand in FY2026 after absorbing USD 82,174 thousand in FY2025, and before those movements conversion was 50.69% in both years, so the underlying rate was stable at about half of Adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F21; calculation F22; calculation F23; calculation F24; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 90

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate and flexible: capital expenditures were 7.28% of trailing net sales and about USD 200 million is planned for FY2027, 19.93% below FY2026, including about USD 80 million already on order; cash interest takes 9.26% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA and cash taxes paid fell 20.26% in FY2026. In the first half of FY2027 operating cash flow fell 10.12% on working capital, but before working-capital movements it grew 12.93%, so the half's weakness is timing and the seasonality that puts 55.08% of annual sales in the first half. Finance lease payments of USD 40,602 thousand in FY2026 and integration and restructuring cash costs sit outside the issuer's free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F04; calculation F20; calculation F06; calculation F09; calculation F07; calculation F29; calculation F08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is moderate. The stormwater industry is highly fragmented with many regional specialists, the company competes with concrete, corrugated steel and PVC producers as well as other HDPE makers, and claims the only national corrugated HDPE footprint; rivalry is mostly on local coverage, availability and price, which limits margin only when volume is weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is low to moderate. Entry needs a plant network that serves a shipping radius of about 250 miles, regulatory approvals from municipalities and state transport departments, and recycled-resin processing know-how, which protects returns on the issuer's installed base without preventing regional entry.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is moderate and price-linked. Concrete, steel and PVC remain the alternatives; thermoplastic pipe has been gaining share on weight, cost and installation, but the filing accepts that a sharp resin rise can leave the company unable to pass costs through because of competing-product pricing, so substitution risk peaks exactly when resin is expensive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high. Two distributors took 25.8% of FY2026 net sales and the ten largest customers about 50%, many without long-term arrangements, and customer consolidation could move volume to competitors; the consequence for creditors is that a single customer decision can move sales and margin within a quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is moderate. Polypropylene resin suppliers are limited and high-density polyethylene suppliers are geographically concentrated, although the company buys from about 450 suppliers, holds multi-year supply agreements and processes its own recycled resin; supplier power therefore shows up as price volatility and a pass-through lag more than as a supply stoppage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three categories are material to credit. Regulatory approvals and stormwater rules decide where products may be used and are a source of market access but also of delay; the economic cycle, interest rates and credit availability drive non-residential, residential and agricultural demand, and about 30% of new single-family homes use onsite wastewater systems, which ties the Wastewater segment to housing; and tariffs on resin or other inputs are a cost risk that the company may not pass on. Social and technological factors are not primary credit drivers on the supplied evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: a national plant and distribution network, procurement scale in resin, high margins and stable underlying cash conversion, regulatory approvals that widen the addressable market, and liquidity with back-ended maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses: customer concentration, a lagged resin pass-through, fixed-cost operating leverage, an intangible-heavy acquisition record that is still being integrated, and a payout policy that has outrun free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality: continued material conversion, cross-selling allied products through NDS and StormTrap, onsite wastewater approvals, and a stated leverage target or slower buyback that would lock in the balance-sheet strength.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken it: a housing or non-residential downturn, a resin or tariff shock that cannot be passed on, customer consolidation, severe weather and climate rules that disrupt operations or raise cost, and debt-funded acquisitions or buybacks beyond what cash flow supports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A first strength is cash generation with flexibility. Free cash flow was 59.12% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2026, 50.69% before working-capital movements, it covered trailing cash interest 5.49 times, and capital expenditure is guided down from USD 249,766 thousand to about USD 200 million, so debt service has a wide cushion and a lever in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F01; calculation F23; calculation F05; calculation F20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second strength is margin level and mix: the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 31.97% over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and Wastewater earned 43.59% against 28.89% in Stormwater, which gives earnings room to absorb a volume or price shock before interest cover is threatened.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third strength is liquidity with back-ended maturities: USD 891.88 million of liquidity at 2026-09-30, only 2.87% of principal due before fiscal 2030 and no bond until 2030-07-15, so refinancing risk is remote for at least two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F10; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 121; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A fourth strength is market position and conversion: management describes a national footprint in a fragmented industry and a continuing shift from concrete, steel and PVC to thermoplastic pipe; this is management language, but the 64 plants, regulatory approvals and 41 distribution centers are documented and support share retention.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A fifth strength is moderate leverage today: net debt was 1.60x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, which is 2.30x pro forma for the StormTrap purchase (agreement dated 2026-10-01) and the repurchase after quarter end, still far below the 4.25x springing covenant level on a different definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A first weakness is volume sensitivity with operating leverage: net sales excluding NDS fell 4.50% in the September 2026 quarter, domestic pipe sales fell 7.59%, and the Stormwater segment margin fell 1.48 percentage points, which shows fixed plant cost and a lagged resin pass-through turning a modest volume fall into margin loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second weakness is financial policy: cash returned to shareholders was 112.22% of free cash flow in the first half of FY2027 and acquisitions plus shareholder returns were 159.53% of free cash flow over FY2025 and FY2026, with no leverage target stated, so the next move can add debt without any limit creditors can see.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third weakness is customer concentration: the two largest distributors took 25.8% of FY2026 net sales and the ten largest customers about 50%, many without long-term arrangements, so one customer decision can move volume and price within a quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A fourth weakness is acquisition integration and asset quality: goodwill and identified intangibles are 78.51% of the NDS price, NDS was left out of the internal control assessment, five NDS entities were held for sale on acquisition and StormTrap is the fourth purchase in two years, so recovery of value from deals is not yet visible in earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A fifth weakness is resin exposure with a pass-through lag: resin is the main variable input, the filing says increases may lag costs and may not be passed on where competing materials cap prices, and the September 2026 gross margin was 1.11 percentage points lower than a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are a full year of NDS, price and mix gains, StormTrap adding engineered stormwater products, flexible capital expenditure and ample liquidity; the headwinds are the volume decline seen in the September 2026 quarter, resin and tariff costs, higher interest cost on the larger debt stack, the seasonally weaker second half, and execution on integrating two large acquisitions. No earnings guidance is published, and the only quantified outlook is capital expenditure of about USD 200 million in FY2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the debt structure is comfortable until the USD 500 million senior notes due 2030-07-15, which fall in fiscal 2031 with 34.27% of principal due by then, and the revolver due 2031-02-27; the structural tailwind is material conversion and wider approvals, and the structural headwind is that repeated acquisition and payout decisions, not business risk, will determine whether leverage stays moderate when those maturities are refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F11; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 121; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most plausible issuer-specific downside begins with a housing and non-residential slowdown in the seasonally weaker second half, coinciding with a resin spike that the company cannot pass on quickly. Pipe and allied volume falls further after the 7.59% drop in domestic pipe sales in the September 2026 quarter, price and mix cannot offset it, and fixed plant costs push gross margin and the Stormwater segment margin down faster than sales, as the 1.11 and 1.48 percentage point falls of the September 2026 quarter already show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F18; calculation F15; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 32; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow falls but stays positive because capital expenditures can be cut from about USD 200 million, working capital releases in a downturn, and the buyback, which with dividends exceeded first-half free cash flow by USD 43,939 thousand, can be stopped, while the dividend is small. The risk is sequencing: if StormTrap closes funded mainly from the revolver while payouts continue, revolver exposure could pass USD 262,500 thousand and bring the 4.25x covenant into force just as earnings fall, and at pro forma net leverage of 2.30x on reported EBITDA there is less room than at 1.60x. Management levers are enough to avoid liquidity distress in this scenario, because liquidity of USD 891.88 million and no bond maturity before 2030 give time, but they would have to be used. The primary downside path is a volume-led fall in margin colliding with leverage raised by acquisitions and buybacks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F19; calculation F12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Advanced Drainage Systems presents a strong business and financial profile supported by high margins, strong and flexible cash generation, ample liquidity and maturities that begin in 2030, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, volume and resin sensitivity, and a financial policy that has spent more than free cash flow on acquisitions and buybacks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate to strong, because underlying conversion is about half of Adjusted EBITDA and capital expenditure can flex. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage at the time of the 2030 notes and 2031 revolver maturities, which is set by the next two years of payout and acquisition decisions. The primary downside path is a volume-led fall in margin meeting higher leverage while covenant terms are not supplied. Further analysis would require covenant and basket terms, StormTrap and NDS earnings and a stated leverage target. Fundamental credit analysis is complete. Top risk: releveraging through acquisitions and buybacks into a softer volume cycle.
